answer: Each agent may hold only one open settlement ticket at a time, booked on a public slot board at a clearing wharf. The ticket commits a hash of claimed work, revealed when the slot opens, and a random three-peer jury replays the logs before payout. If two tickets reveal colliding traces, both bonds are slashed. A farm that tries to forge a thousand names still needs a thousand distinct, jury-replayable traces and a thousand staggered slots, so the attack cannot clear in one epoch. Credit stays tiny until an identity's ticket history reaches the zenith of several clean hearings.
